statement: For a fundamental localizer $W$ and a small category $S$, put \[ W^{\mathrm{pre}}_S=\{u:X\to Y\text{ over }S:\ s\backslash u\in W\text{ for all }s\in S\}, \qquad W^{\mathrm{co}}_S=\{u:X\to Y\text{ over }S:\ u/s\in W\text{ for all }s\in S\}. \] Both are weakly saturated classes contained in the total class $W_S$. Opposition gives an isomorphism of relative categories $(\Cat/S,W^{\mathrm{pre}}_S)\cong (\Cat/S^{\op},W^{\mathrm{co}}_{S^{\op}})$. For $W=W_\infty$, their enhanced localizations are, respectively, $\Fun(NS^{\op},\Spaces)$ and $\Fun(NS,\Spaces)$. The value of the first classifier at $s$ is $B(s\backslash X)$; the value of the second is $B(X/s)$. In the notation of XII ms.~222, $W^{\mathrm g}_S$ is the second class.
notes: Presheaf test is s\X; covariant test is X/s.

statement: Let $S$ be a small quasicategory and let $u:X\to Y$ be any map of simplicial sets over $S$; neither $X$ nor $Y$ is assumed fibrant. Then $u$ is a covariant equivalence exactly when \[ X\times_S S_{/s}\longrightarrow Y\times_S S_{/s} \] is a weak homotopy equivalence for every vertex $s$. Replacing $S_{/s}$ by $S_{s/}$ gives the contravariant test. For an arbitrary simplicial base these statements hold with a right, respectively left, fibrant replacement $\widetilde S_{/s}\to S$, respectively $\widetilde S_{s/}\to S$, of the vertex map in place of the literal slice.
notes: All total objects allowed; literal slices require a quasicategorical base.

statement: For every small ordinary category $S$, the ordinary nerve induces equivalences \[ (\Cat/S)[(W^{\mathrm{co}}_S)^{-1}]_\infty \simeq (\sSet/NS)[(W^{\mathrm{cov}})^{-1}]_\infty \simeq\Fun(NS,\Spaces), \] and, by opposition, \[ (\Cat/S)[(W^{\mathrm{pre}}_S)^{-1}]_\infty \simeq (\sSet/NS)[(W^{\mathrm{contra}})^{-1}]_\infty \simeq\Fun(NS^{\op},\Spaces). \] Here $W=W_\infty$. These are equivalences of infinity-categories and therefore of homotopy categories. The last comparison is implemented by the straightening--unstraightening Quillen equivalence. No model structure on $\Cat/S$ with the ordinary nerve as a right Quillen functor is asserted.
notes: Enhanced localization equivalence; no unsupported Quillen claim for the raw nerve.

statement: Lead~1 is false for arbitrary simplicial bases when its tests use literal simplicial slices. Let $S=\Lambda^2_1$, with nondegenerate edges $01$ and $12$ and no $02$ edge. The map $\{0\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{\{0,1\}}$ over $S$ is a covariant equivalence, but its pullback along $S_{/2}\to S$ is $\varnothing\to\{1\}$ and is not a weak homotopy equivalence.
notes: Explicit inner-horn base; finite simplex intersections checked.

statement: For $p:A\to B$ in $\Cat$, Grothendieck's $W_\infty$-properness is equivalent to properness of $Np$ in \citet[Definition 4.4.1]{BCCisinski2019}, and to smoothness of $Np$ in \citet[Definition 4.1.2.9]{BCLurie2009}. Grothendieck's $W_\infty$-smoothness corresponds to Cisinski-smoothness and to the opposite of Lurie's smoothness. Thus the two cited books use opposite names. The equivalences hold in both directions for all ordinary functors, without a fibration hypothesis.
notes: Grothendieck-proper equals Lurie-smooth; ordinary nerve criterion unaffected by erratum.

statement: Let $\widehat{\mathcal L}_{\mathrm{co}}$ consist of those $p:A\to B$ for which every strict base change $p_T:A\times_BT\to T$ preserves $W^{\mathrm{co}}_T$ under raw pullback. Then \[ \widehat{\mathcal L}_{\mathrm{co}}=\Liss_W, \qquad \widehat{\mathcal L}_{\mathrm{pre}}=\Prop_W. \] No accessibility assumption is needed. In particular the equality left open at XII ms.~222 has an affirmative answer in the manuscript's covariant variance; it is not the assertion that all raw inverse images are homotopical.
notes: Maximal class equality settled with covariant manuscript variance, without accessibility.

statement: There are strict inclusions \[ \{\text{Grothendieck bifibrations}\}\subsetneq \Liss_{W_\infty}\cap\Prop_{W_\infty}\subsetneq\Fib_{W_\infty}. \] For simplicial sets, Cisinski-smooth and Cisinski-proper maps likewise lie in the intrinsic class preserving all weak homotopy equivalences under strict pullback. The analogous inclusion for a larger fundamental localizer is generally false.
notes: Diamond and V finite separators; strict pullback class distinguished from bifibrations.

statement: For a small category $C$ and $x\in C$, let $E_x(C)$ have as objects the functors $\gamma:J\to C$, where $J$ has objects $\mathbb Z$ and arrows $2i\to2i-1$, $2i\to2i+1$, which are constantly $x$ with identity arrows at the left end and constantly some object at the right end. Morphisms are natural transformations whose eventual left component is $1_x$; composition is componentwise. Then $q:E_x(C)\to C$, taking the eventual right value, is $W_\infty$-smooth and proper, $BE_x(C)$ is weakly contractible, and its strict fibres are the homotopy fibres of $\{x\}\to BC$.
notes: Fully specified integer-fence category; all lift contractions proved.

statement: For a fundamental localizer $W$ in the relative-Theorem-A convention, \[ \Liss_W\cap\Prop_W\subset\Fib_W \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad W=W_\infty\ \text{or}\ W=\operatorname{Mor}(\Cat). \] Accessibility is not required. Thus the tentative complementarity at XII ms.~225--226 is false for every proper enlargement of $W_\infty$ other than the total class.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: XII ms.225--226; POLES E.5; STRATA G.5
notes: Only minimal and total localizers; no accessibility.

statement: For every $n\geq0$, $\Liss_{W_n}\cap\Prop_{W_n}$ is not contained in $\Fib_{W_n}$. For $n=0$ a finite witness is the regular covering $EC_2\to BC_2$. For $n\geq1$ B.8 supplies a completely specified witness with base the face poset of the boundary of an $(n+2)$-simplex.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: XII ms.225--226; POLES C.8--C.9; STRATA G.3--G.4
notes: W0 finite covering; all finite truncations by specified sphere path model.

statement: Let $E$ be any nonzero spectrum, with no connectivity assumption, and let $W_E$ mean equivalence on $E\wedge\Sigma^\infty(-)_+$. The three-sheeted action-groupoid covering in the prompt is both $W_E$-smooth and $W_E$-proper, but is not in $\Fib_{W_E}$.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: XII ms.225--226; POLES C.10; PATHS E.9
notes: One covering and one free-group endomorphism work for every nonzero spectrum, including nonconnective spectra.

statement: Put $W_{\mathbb Q}^{\mathrm{lc}}=W_{D(\mathbb Q)}^{\mathrm{lc}}$, where locally constant diagrams are coherent diagrams of unbounded rational complexes. There is a finite bifibration $p:H\to K$, with $14$ objects and $100$ arrows upstairs, which belongs to both $\Liss_W\cap\Prop_W$ for every fundamental localizer $W$, but belongs to neither $\Fib_{W_1}$ nor $\Fib_{W_{\mathbb Q}^{\mathrm{lc}}}$. The functor $p$ itself belongs to $W_{\mathbb Q}^{\mathrm{lc}}$.
notes: Finite gerbe and self-pullback; exact nonabelian group presentations checked.

statement: Every covering of ordinary categories, meaning a discrete fibration and a discrete opfibration, belongs to $\Fib_{W_1}$ and to $\Fib_{W_{\mathbb Q}^{\mathrm{lc}}}$. In particular the three-sheeted covering of B.11 belongs to these two intrinsic classes, although it belongs to no $\Fib_{W_E}$ for $E\ne0$. The endpoint map of B.8 with $C=BC_2$ lies in the same two intrinsic classes, while it fails to lie in the rational-homology intrinsic class.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: GALOIS D.3; POLES C.10; PATHS E.9
notes: Coverings preserve W1 and rational local-system equivalences, unlike all homology localizers.

statement: Let $\mathcal D$ be the derivator of a nonterminal presentable infinity-category, and use presheaf variance. Define a cohomological $\mathcal D$-fibration by requiring, after every strict base change, that right Kan extension sends every locally constant coefficient to a locally constant coefficient and has the canonical strict-fibre formula. This class and $\Prop_{W_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{lc}}}$ are not contained in one another. Dually, the homological class and $\Liss_{W_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{lc}}}$ are not contained in one another. In particular both conclusions apply to sets, spaces, and rational complexes.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: I ms.117--118; GALOIS D.2 and D.9
notes: Neither containment for proper versus strong cohomological, and dually.

statement: The following table evaluates the maps specified in GALOIS D.3--D.5 for $W=W_1$ and $W=W_{\mathbb Q}^{\mathrm{lc}}$. A pair of entries gives these two localizers in that order; a single entry applies to both. Here ``smooth'' and ``proper'' always use the same $W$ as the intrinsic column. \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c|c} \text{specified map}&W\text{-smooth}&W\text{-proper}&\Fib_W\\\hline \mathrm{D.3}:p:E\to B&\text{yes}&\text{yes}&\text{yes}\\ \mathrm{D.3}:q:B\to[1]&\text{no}&\text{yes}&\text{no}\\ \mathrm{D.3}:qp&\text{no}&\text{yes}&\text{no}\\ \mathrm{D.4}:p:E\to B&\text{yes}&\text{yes}&\text{no}\\ \mathrm{D.4}:q:B\to[1]&\text{no}&\text{yes}&(\text{yes},\text{no})\\ \mathrm{D.4}:qp&\text{no}&\text{yes}&\text{no}\\ \mathrm{D.5}:H\to K&\text{yes}&\text{yes}&\text{no}\\ \mathrm{D.5}:q:R\to[1]&\text{no}&\text{yes}&\text{no} \end{array} \]
notes: Every named finite map tested for W1 and rational locally constant complexes.

statement: If $W$ is an accessible fundamental localizer, let $\Spaces_W$ be the presentable localization of spaces corresponding to $W$. Then \[ (\Cat/S)[(W^{\mathrm{pre}}_S)^{-1}]_\infty \simeq\Fun(NS^{\op},\Spaces_W),\qquad (\Cat/S)[(W^{\mathrm{co}}_S)^{-1}]_\infty \simeq\Fun(NS,\Spaces_W). \] For an arbitrary fundamental localizer the relative definitions, the opposition isomorphism, B.6 and B.9 remain valid without accessibility. A presentable coefficient category in the displayed formulas is not asserted without the accessibility hypothesis.
notes: Accessible coefficient presentation; no presentability claimed for arbitrary inaccessible W.

statement: For $n\geq0$, a functor $p:T\to B$ lies in $\Fib_{W_n}$ if and only if, for every $X\to B$, the canonical map \[ \tau_{\leq n}B(T\times_BX)\longrightarrow \tau_{\leq n}BT\times_{\tau_{\leq n}BB}\tau_{\leq n}BX \] is an equivalence of $n$-types. The pullback on the right is a homotopy pullback in $\Spaces_{\leq n}$. For $n=0$ this is equivalent to the following elementary pair of conditions. For every connected component $B_j$ of $B$, write $T_j=T\times_BB_j$. Then $\pi_0(T_b)\to\pi_0(T_j)$ must be bijective for each $b\in B_j$; and for every arrow $\beta:b\to b'$ and every component $c$ of $T_j$ there must be an arrow of $T$ over $\beta$ in component $c$.
notes: Proper-localizer hypothesis explicitly verified; elementary W0 criterion also proved.

statement: For every spectrum $E$, $\Fib_{W_E}$ contains product projections and inclusions of unions of connected components, together with their closure under composition, strict base change and retracts. It is contained in the class of $p:T\to B$ for which every inclusion \[ T_{\sigma(i)}\longrightarrow T\times_B[m], \qquad \sigma:[m]\to B,quad 0\leq i\leq m, \] is an $E$-equivalence. For $E\ne0$ this upper bound is strict.
notes: Bounds for intrinsic homology fibrations; simplex tests insufficient.

statement: Let $\mathcal P(C)$ be the category of all eventually constant diagrams $J\to C$ on the integer fence of B.8, with all natural transformations. Write $\sigma,\beta$ for the eventual left and right values. Then $(\sigma,\beta):\mathcal P(C)\to C\times C$ is smooth and proper for $W_\infty$, and therefore for every fundamental localizer. For every $f:A\to C$, the functors \[ E(f)=A\times_{C,\sigma}\mathcal P(C),\qquad i_f(a)=(a,\operatorname{const}_{f(a)}),\qquad p_f(a,\gamma)=\beta(\gamma) \] give $f=p_fi_f$, with $i_f\in W_\infty$ and $p_f$ smooth and proper. All formulas are natural in strictly commuting squares. For $C=[1]$, the endpoint functor is neither a Grothendieck fibration nor an opfibration. Thus the verified fence construction in PATHS has exactly the asserted homotopical properties, without being a bifibration.
notes: Independent all-ended fence proof and functorial factorization; not a strict bifibration.

statement: Use the all-type category $\operatorname{Ch}(C)$ with objects finite oriented interval diagrams and morphisms $(h,\eta)$, where $h$ is an endpoint-preserving, weakly monotone functor of their interval types and $\eta:\gamma\Rightarrow\delta h$. Its endpoint map is smooth for every $C$, but for $C=[1]$ it is not proper and is neither a Grothendieck opfibration nor a fibration. The conclusion cannot be transferred from B.19 by calling both objects ``path categories'' or by reversing the path word.
notes: Smoothness proved by padding and contractible slice; empty outgoing lift and two incoming type maps refute stronger claims.

statement: For the one-object category of the monoid $R=\{1,e_{00},e_{01},e_{10},e_{11}\}$ with $e_{ij}e_{kl}=e_{il}$ and $1r=r1=r$, it remains unsettled here whether the local system of path spaces has a representative by a strict Grothendieck bifibration with contractible total category. The eventual fence endpoint functor is not such a representative.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: STRATA E.11; PATHS E.6 and E.11
notes: Open only for existence of some alternative bifibration; standard path obstruction checked.

statement: For every simplicial base $S$, let $W^{\mathrm{cov}}_S$ and $W^{\mathrm{contra}}_S$ denote the actual covariant and contravariant equivalences. The maps whose every base change preserves these classes under raw pullback are, respectively, Cisinski-smooth and Cisinski-proper maps. Moreover the manuscript's universal test recipe gives exactly \[ W^{\Liss_{\mathrm{Cis}}}_S=W^{\mathrm{cov}}_S, \qquad W^{\Prop_{\mathrm{Cis}}}_S=W^{\mathrm{contra}}_S. \] Thus opposition gives a perfect duality over $S^{\op}$ for every simplicial base, although B.4 refutes the version using literal slices at an arbitrary base. For accessible $W$, replace fibrewise equivalences of spaces by fibrewise $W$-equivalences after left or right fibrant replacement. These two accessible localizations classify diagrams with values in $\Spaces_W$ on the directed infinity-category presented by $S$ or its opposite, and their restrictions to ordinary nerves are B.16. Their universal raw-pullback classes contain the minimal smooth and proper classes. Complementarity with intrinsic total $W$-equivalences holds for these classes only for $W_\infty$ and the total localizer.
notes: All simplicial bases using true covariant structures; accessible coefficient extension and rigidity.
